title: Software packages and APT
subtitle: RPM/DEB families, apt-get, apt-cache, and sources.list — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Software packed in an archive so a package management system (or self-contained installer) can install it
cards.notes: You do not copy random binaries onto a server — you install a package; the manager tracks files, versions, and deps.

cards.meaning: Tools that install, upgrade, configure, and remove packages automatically — including dependencies
*.rpm
*.deb
Low-level tool on Red Hat–based systems — talks to a single file on disk
cards.notes: RPM = Red Hat Package Manager; started at Red Hat, used by many distros.

cards.meaning: Low-level tool on Debian–based systems — talks to a single file on disk
High-level CLI package manager for RPM-compatible systems (Yellowdog Updater, Modified); GNU GPL
cards.notes: Talks to repositories, resolves deps, downloads, then calls rpm. Newer RHEL uses dnf; this course names yum.

cards.meaning: High-level tools on Debian-based systems — repositories, deps, then dpkg
cards.notes: Interview: yum is to rpm as apt is to dpkg. APT = Advanced Packaging Tool.

cards.meaning: Low-level = single file on disk; high-level = repositories, resolve deps, download, then call low-level
cards.notes: Red Hat = RPM + yum. Debian/Ubuntu = DEB + apt.

cards.meaning: From Debra, then partner of Debian founder Ian Murdock (same Deb as Debian)
Retrieve new lists of packages (refresh what repos offer); does not upgrade installed software
cards.notes: Memory hook: update = refresh the catalog.

cards.meaning: Upgrade already installed packages
cards.notes: upgrade/install = change what is on disk.

cards.meaning: Install new packages by package name, not the .deb filename
cards.notes: Install nginx, not nginx.deb, when using apt-get.

cards.meaning: Remove packages; config files may stay
cards.notes: remove keeps configs; purge does not.

cards.meaning: Remove packages and their config files
Verify there are no broken dependencies
Low-level tool that reads APT’s binary cache and queries it; does not install anything
cards.notes: Memory hook: apt-get changes the system. apt-cache only looks up the cache.

cards.meaning: Search the package list with a regex
Readable record for the package
General information for one package
Raw dependency information
Main file where APT reads repository lists
Extra repo lists — one file per vendor (Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, …)
cards.notes: Memory hook: extra vendors drop a file here. Run apt-get update after adding a repo.

cards.meaning: Binary packages
cards.example: deb http://ftp.by.debian.org/debian/ buster main non-free contrib

cards.meaning: Source packages
cards.example: deb-src http://ftp.by.debian.org/debian/ buster main non-free contrib

cards.meaning: Repository mirror
Debian release codename (here: Debian 10)
cards.notes: Typical extra stanzas: buster/updates (security), buster-updates, buster-backports.

cards.meaning: Repository components (free vs contrib vs non-free)
